correctness.rationale: For any positive-area measurable X, closed convexification preserves minimal width and can only increase area. Bounding rectangle in a minimizing width direction gives A(X)<=ω(X)D(Ω). A diameter chord pq and off-chord interior point r provide a triangular section of length D(1−s/h), so 0<t<h slices satisfy ω(X_t)/A(X_t)<=1/[D(1−t/2h)] ->1/D. Equality would force a positive-width D-by-ω rectangle within Ω, whose diagonal exceeds D(Ω), contradiction. Noncompact X is handled by closed hull.
residual_risks: Elementary inequality may appear under a different width/diameter functional name in older convex-geometric literature.
Value/attainment is only for the unrestricted positive-area measurable subset class; extra topology or minimum area restrictions can change the result.
